messages.subject: wall time
parts:
Sometimes people write in with comments about the speed of Stan in particular examples. Does everyone know that rstan (and, I think, the other versions of Stan) can be configured so it runs in parallel by default? My laptop has 4 processors and when I run Stan from R, it automatically runs 4 chains, one in each processor. This makes a big difference!

In Rstan:
library("rstan")
rstan_options(auto_write = TRUE)
options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())

Anyway, probably most of you know this, but just in case you don’t . . . you want to do this. A factor of 4 is nothing to scoff at!

A
